text: At seventeen minutes past ten on a February night, a turboprop on approach to Buffalo was five miles from the runway. Everything on board was working.

text: On the pilot's display there is a vertical strip of numbers. Beside it sits a red and black bar.

text: The bar marks the speed below which the wing stops flying. When the aeroplane slows, it climbs toward the number.

text: It is the only warning on the aeroplane that arrives early, and it arrives silently, and it arrives in the one place a pilot is trained to look.

text: The low-speed cue appeared on the display. The bar began to climb. And nothing happened for eighteen seconds.

text: Eighteen seconds is a long time in a cockpit. It is long enough to push two levers forward.
